title: Air and Missile Defense (AMD) Systems Tactician
raw_text:
8-140K. Military Occupational Specialty 140K--Air and Missile Defense (AMD) Systems
Tactician
    a. Licensing/certification requirement. None.
    b. Prerequisites. AR 601 series.
    c. MOS 140K. MOS 140K is an accession MOS. The Enlisted feeder MOSs are 14E, 14G,
14H, 14P and 14T. The United States Army (USA) Officer feeder AOC is: 14A (O2-O3). The
United States Marine Corps (USMC) Enlisted feeder MOSs are: 72XX.
    d. Associated SQI.
         (1) 0--No special qualifications.
         (2) 8--Instructor.
         (3) P--Parachutist.
         (4) T--Transition (personnel only).
         (5) Z--Research, Development, Test, and Evaluation Technician.
    e. Associated ASI. (Note: Refer to table 6-6 for (Listing of universal ASI’s associated with all
warrant officer MOS)).
        (1) Q6--Protection Cell Operations (personnel only).
         (2) T3--Ground-based Midcourse Defense (GMD) System.
         (3) T4--Air Defense Artillery Fire Control Officer (ADAFCO).
         (4) T5--Patriot Top Gun.
          (5) 2N – GMD Analyst (Effective 202710)
         (6) 7B—THAAD Tactician.
    f. Qualifications.
         (1) WO1 must--
               (a) Complete the AMD Warrant Officer Basic Course.
               (b) Be a U.S. citizen. Qualify for a security eligibility of SECRET.
               (c) Have normal vision correctable to 20/20; normal color discrimination; full use of
both hands; and have normal hearing per AR 40-501.
               (d) Have a physical profile that allows assignment to remote locations.
               (e) A physical demands rating of moderate (Gold).
               (f) A minimum OPAT score of Standing Long Jump (LJ) – 120 cm, Seated Power
Throw (PT) – 350 cm, Strength Deadlift (SD) – 120 lbs., and Interval Aerobic Run (IR) – 0036
shuttles in Physical Demand Category “”Moderate” (Gold).
         (2) CW2 must--
               (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f(1).
               (b) Complete the Common Core & AMD Systems Tactician Warrant Officer
Intermediate Course (WOIC).
         (3) CW3 must--
               (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f(2).
               (b) Obtain and maintain a TS/SCI security clearance.
               (c) Complete the Common Core & Warrant Officer Advanced Course (WOAC).
         (4) CW4 must--
               (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f(3).
               (b) Complete the Common Core & Warrant Officer Senior Course (WOSC).
         (5) CW5 must—
               (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f(4).
               (b) Complete the Warrant Officer Mastery Course (WOMC).
    g. Duties.
         (1) WO1/CW2—
               (a) Provides leadership and oversees the battery Fire Control crew functions:
identification, surveillance, weapon control, integration, and fire control.
               (b) Conducts air battle management, and Air Defense operations as battery Fire
Control Officer (FCO).
               (c) Ensures tracks are properly identified and engaged in accordance with published
criteria.
               (d) Assesses overall defense effectiveness of assigned assets, and evaluate risk to
defended assets.
               (e) Communicates with battalion fire control officer.
              (f) Monitors engagement operations, and prevent unnecessary multiple
engagements.
              (g) Advises the commander on readiness aspects of march order, emplacement and
capabilities and limitations of the Air Defense weapon systems.
              (h) Implements and ensure compliance with proper safety and security procedures
applicable to the AMD weapons systems.
              (i) Assists platoon leaders in operator/crew training.
              (j) Conducts tactical training for crew certifications.
              (k) Serves as battery standardization officer.
         (2) CW3--
              (a) Perform duties described in paragraph g (1).
              (b) Conducts air battle management, and Air Defense operations as battalion fire
control officer.
              (b) Provide AMD weapons systems peculiar tactical assistance, reporting guidance,
and direction to subordinate elements.
              (c) Advise the commander or staff officers on AMD weapons systems capabilities and
limitations.
              (d) Evaluates, trains, and validates unit readiness for the commander.
              (e) Coordinates total package fielding and the effects of modifications to the AMD
weapons systems and trains new doctrinal concepts.
              (f) Serves as an instructor, writer, training developer and evaluator for MOS related
service schools.
              (g) Serves as the battalion standardization officer.
         (3) CW4--
              (a) Perform duties described in paragraph g (2).
              (b) Performs duties as ADAFCO at ADA brigade and Army Air and Missile Defense
Command (AAMDC) levels.
              (c) Serve as Project Manager on New/Improved AMD weapon systems fielding.
              (d) Provide leadership, guidance, tactical input, and direction to subordinate
elements, staff agencies, and field commanders up to and including Brigade/Corps level.

               (e) Serves as a combat developer for the Capabilities, Development and Integration
Directorate.
              (f) Serves as the brigade standardization officer.
         (4) CW5--
              (a) Perform duties described in paragraph g (3).
              (b) Develop, review and update the life cycle management of AMD warrant officers.
              (c) Advise the Commandant and Assistant Commandant at the Army Air Defense
Artillery School on all matters pertaining to AMD warrant officers.
              (d) Provide leadership, guidance, technical input, and direction to subordinate
elements, staff agencies, field commanders at theater level, and interfaces with senior leadership
in a joint/combined environment.
              (e) Coordinates training, and evaluations for Air and Missile Defense (AMD) systems.
    h. Grading and position titles. Authorized position titles are provided in tables 6-2 and 6-3. The
following grades are used to code positions into one of four definable skill levels: W2 equals
WO1/CW2; W3 equals CW3; W4 equals CW4; and W5 equals CW5. The grades are listed in the
following standards of grade tables:
         (1) Table 8-140K-1. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
         (2) Table 8-140K-2. Standards of grade TDA.
    i. Physical demands rating and qualifications for initial award of MOS. Air and Missile Defense
(AMD) Systems Tactician must possess the following qualifications:
         (1) A physical demands rating of light.
         (2) A physical profile of 222221.
         (3) Normal color vision.
         (4) Possess normal dexterity in both hands.
 (5) A security eligibility of SECRET is required for the initial award of the MOS.
 (6) A security eligibility of TS/SCI is required for CW3-CW5.
 (7) A U.S. citizen.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
